Commission an add-on

If Archie can’t do it yet, we’ll build it.

Every “easy” AI tool is easy because it’s limited. Archie is easy because we did the hard part first, and when you reach the edge of what it can do, that edge moves. Tell us what you need. We’ll scope it and build it. It’s yours, and it goes on the marketplace, so the next person who needs it doesn’t have to ask.

Tell us what you need
How it works

Three steps, and only the first is yours.

A commission starts as a conversation, not a project plan. You bring the need; we do the rest.

1

Tell us what you need

Describe it in plain language: the thing you keep doing by hand, the app your agent doesn’t know yet. No spec required.

2

We scope it and quote it

We work out exactly what it takes and put a price on it. You know the cost before we write a line of it.

3

We build it, and it’s yours

Your agent picks up the new ability, and the add-on joins the marketplace for everyone who needs it after you, and you earn 25% of the proceeds from every sale of it.

Quoted per add-on: scope first, price before any work starts.

What it can be

Any kind of add-on.

A commission can take the shape of any kind of add-on. If you’re not sure which one fits, that’s what scoping is for. New to add-ons? Start with the basics.

A skill

Something new your agent can do: the app or tool it doesn’t know how to work with yet.

A routine

Something it does on its own, on your schedule: the report you wish landed every Monday.

A personality

How your agent talks to you: a voice and tone shaped around how you like to work.

Why we work this way

Your one-off makes the whole thing better.

Every commissioned add-on becomes a marketplace listing, so the marketplace grows with real demand: things people actually needed, not things we guessed they might. And the thing you paid to have built pays you back every time someone else needs it too.

It’s the same move that built Archie in the first place: we kept hand-building the same setups for clients until we turned them into a product. That’s our whole story; commissions are the next chapter of it.
